families.family: matmul_ogs MoE GEMM, non-persistent (gather/scatter/ragged/MX/flex)
families.reference: candidate (lib ref): matmul.py::matmul_torch (+apply_precision); dense-only subset = a.double() @ b.double() + bias
open_decisions: gather_indx row mapping (no -1 handling) and scatter_indx (-1 = drop, overwrite not accumulate, collisions undefined)
ragged metadata format for ragged-M (MoE) and ragged-K (dW = X^T dY per slice) modes, incl. padded/unused rows
MX operand formats: mxfp4/mxfp8 values, E8M0 vs E4M3 (NVFP4) block scales, block size 32/16, per-row tensor scales, NVFP4->MXFP8 requantization (sm100)
swizzled value/scale layouts (HOPPER_VALUE, HOPPER/BLACKWELL/CDNA4/CDNA5 scales)
flexpoint per-tensor/per-batch scales: expected/actual/checksum semantics, saturate_inf
epilogue order: acc*xs*ws + bias*beta, *out_alpha, fused activation (reduction_n), *gamma, + c_acc_in*acc_scale, then flex/MX output quantization
accumulation precision: fp32 acc (fp64 only if both fp64), TF32 rounding of fp32 inputs when allow_tf32 (default True), max_num_imprecise_acc
split-K partials reduced by reduce() with activation moved there
fused multi-GPU output comm (map_dst_coord, n_reduce_shards)
spec_sources: NVIDIA NVFP4 (E2M1 + E4M3 block-16 scale) documentation
families.notes: domain: wrapper picks _p_matmul only if is_tma_compliant(), which is False below sm90, so on sm86 every call runs _matmul; dense bf16/fp16/fp32/fp64 path is plain tl.dot. fp32 inputs are rounded to TF32 by default (allow_tf32=True). Gathered row offsets wrap modulo slice size (offs % eM) and are masked on store. Bias is added only by split k=0; Betas scale bias only; Gammas are applied after the activation. deviation: matmul_torch dequantizes MX operands with the Triton kernel upcast_from_mxfp, so the library reference is not independent of the library's Triton code; it also ignores out_alpha, fused activation/epilogue, c_acc_in, tensor scales and fused comm, and zero-fills rows that the kernel leaves unwritten (ragged-M padding rows, dropped scatter rows); docstring writes Y[idx] += but kernel overwrites. MX paths use tl.dot_scaled (compiler-decomposed below sm100; per audit rule treat as not-sm86); fp8e4nv operands need sm89+.

families.family: masked/scaled reduction over one axis (split-K reducer, MoE combine)

MX/NVFP4 output quantization (scale rounding, e2m1 RTNE, nibble packing, value pack factor)

postprocess_fn1 (grouped reduction_n, e.g. swiglu) / postprocess_fn2 closures
unpadded_batch_size: rows past it are not written
summation order (bitmap path sums active inputs in ascending k)
families.notes: domain: x must be 3D; mask/scale broadcast via stride 0; compute dtype fp32 (fp64 when x is fp64); masked-out entries contribute 0. deviation: reduce_torch ignores unpadded_batch_size and x_global_scale; kernel leaves rows >= unpadded uninitialized (torch.empty). mxfp8 output path needs fp8e4nv (sm89+).

families.family: reduce row scheduler (active-input counts + heavy-first row order)
families.reference: ActiveInputCounts = (mask!=0).sum(reduction dim).to(int16); RowIdxs: no lib ref
open_decisions: exact RowIdxs permutation depends on BLOCK_M/BLOCK_S0/grid (per-CTA strided row sets reordered as >=4,3,2,<=1 active inputs, stable) vs only requiring a valid per-CTA permutation
rows beyond UnpaddedBatchSize are not written
families.notes: Internal helper for the _reduce_forward bitmap path (per-row mask, stride_m1==0, K<=32). domain: mask loaded with K <= BLOCK_K.

families.family: reduce backward
families.reference: candidate: autograd of reduce_torch: dx[k,s0,s1] = dy[s0, s1//REDUCTION_N] * e8m0(xmx) * x_flex * scale * (mask!=0)
open_decisions: gradient through postprocess_fn1 is taken as a grouped-sum broadcast regardless of the actual fn
x_global_scale and output flex scales are ignored
no gradient for MX-quantized outputs (raises)
rows >= unpadded_batch_size left unwritten
families.notes: Inherits forward conventions. deviation: dx allocated with torch.empty, so skipped rows are garbage.

families.family: top-k routing (sorted top-k + optional softmax + bitmatrix)
open_decisions: tie-breaking: smaller expert index wins
total order on float bit patterns (-0.0 < +0.0, +NaN largest, -NaN smallest) vs torch.topk
outputs sorted by value descending
softmax over the k selected logits in fp32, cast to x.dtype
index dtype int16
bitmatrix format: uint32 words, bit j of word w = expert 32w+j, transposed storage with rows padded to 32
provided y_indx mode: gather at given indices without re-sorting
rows >= n_rows left untouched
all_gather to symmetric-memory peers
families.notes: domain: 2D input, dim=1, n_cols < 32768, k <= n_cols; padded columns masked to key 0. deviation: topk_torch ranks with argsort(-x, stable), so +0/-0 ties and NaN ordering differ from the kernel's bit-key order; topk_torch fills rows >= n_rows (x[n_rows:, :k], index -1) while the kernel leaves them uninitialized.

families.family: top-k backward (softmax gradient scattered to selected experts)
families.reference: candidate: y=softmax(x.gather(1,idx).double(),-1); dx=zeros_like(x).scatter(1, idx, y*(dy-(y*dy).sum(-1,keepdim=True)) if apply_softmax else dy)
open_decisions: inherits index set/order from forward
duplicate indices in user-provided y_indx (last write wins)
rows >= n_rows not written
families.notes: deviation: dx = torch.empty_like(x), so rows >= n_rows are uninitialized; softmax recomputed in fp32.

families.family: SwiGLU (GPT-OSS variant, interleaved gate/linear, clamp limit, flexpoint)
families.reference: candidate (lib ref): swiglu.py::swiglu_torch: g=a[...,::2].clamp(max=limit); l=a[...,1::2].clamp(-limit,limit); g*torch.sigmoid(alpha*g)*(l+1)
open_decisions: interleaved layout: even columns = gate, odd = linear
asymmetric clamp (gate upper only, linear both sides)
'+1' on the linear branch
flexpoint: input scale applied before clamp, output divided by expected scale, actual_scale absmax atomics, saturate_inf
routing_data n_tokens limits rows (rest unwritten)
spec_sources: openai/gpt-oss reference model (SwiGLU with alpha, limit)
families.notes: domain: last dim even and contiguous; compute fp32; out dtype = a.dtype. deviation: sigmoid via exp2_ftz (flushes denormals); swiglu_torch has no flex support. Plain (no-flex) mode is fully fixed by swiglu_torch.

families.family: masked compaction of top-k (value,index) rows by bitmask
families.reference: keep=((bitmask.gather(1, yi.long()//32) >> (yi.long()%32)) & 1).bool(); order=(~keep).int().argsort(1, stable=True); out_v=torch.where(keep.gather(1,order), yv.gather(1,order), sentinel); out_i likewise  [= compaction.py::compaction_torch]
families.notes: domain: K = yi.shape[1] must be a power of two; yv/yi rows assumed contiguous (kernel ignores their strides); sentinel cast to yv dtype; indices < 32*bitmask.shape[1].

families.family: bitmatrix column counts (expert histogram) + per-32-row partials
families.notes: Despite the name it returns per-column sums. n_rows may be a device scalar; out-of-range rows read as 0; int32 atomics (exact).

families.family: bitmatrix metadata (col-sorted / row-sorted nonzero indices)
open_decisions: stable order within each column (by row-major flat index)
-1 sentinel padding of col_sorted_indx/row_sorted_indx
precondition: bitmatrix and nonzero_indx encode the same sets (counts come from the bitmap, positions from the indices)
limits: column index < 65535, per-block entries <= 32768
families.notes: Stage 1 = exclusive scans of partial column sums (in place), col_offs, memset to -1; stage 2 = block-local stable sort + keyed scan. MoE gather/scatter index construction.

families.family: ragged tensor metadata (slice/block offsets, packed block schedule)

max_n_blocks bound / truncation
exclusive cumsums with total in the last slot
families.notes: domain: requires sum(slice_sizes) <= n_total_rows; otherwise the compute kernel writes schedule entries past max_n_blocks (no bound check) where the torch ref truncates. slice ids < 65536.

families.family: ragged tensor metadata remap (drop/renumber slices)

trailing block_offs slot = number of kept blocks

families.family: expert-parallel token dispatch/combine over symmetric memory
open_decisions: expert->rank ownership bitmask (expert owned by no rank maps to rank 0 because rank = sum(r*owned))
destination row indexing via gate_indx/topk_indx (flat positions) and token partition n_tokens_local*rank
rows never written in destination buffers
duplicate destinations and peer write ordering (barrier after launch)

families.family: quantize to MX (mxfp4/mxfp8 with E8M0 scales; NVFP4 with E4M3 scales)
open_decisions: scale rounding: default ROUND_UP 2^ceil(log2(amax/max_q)) vs OCP ROUND_DOWN floor(log2(amax/max_pow2_q)); ROUND_NEAREST for E4M3 scales
all-zero block: scale byte 0 and quant scale 0
e2m1 RTNE with saturation to +-6 and subnormal handling
fp8 element conversion satfinite
nibble packing (even element in low nibble)
NaN/Inf inputs in block max
NVFP4 block 16 E4M3 scale without global scale
padding exclusion from amax
spec_sources: OCP Microscaling Formats (MX) v1.0 spec (scale computation and element conversion sections)
families.notes: sm86 covers mxfp4 + E8M0 (bit-manipulation e2m1 encoder used below sm100) and e5m2; e4m3 values or E4M3 scales need sm89+. domain: quant axis divisible by microblock size; output value stride 1 on quant axis; src bf16/fp16/fp32.

families.family: dequantize from MX (mxfp4/mxfp8 values, E8M0 or E4M3 scales)

tensor_scale post-multiply (torch wrapper)

families.notes: Host TensorDescriptor is rewritten to pointer loads below sm90 (nvidia compiler make_ttir), so mxfp4/e5m2 paths run on sm86; e4m3 needs sm89+. deviation: kernel clamps after scaling, so e5m2 +-Inf come out as +-max finite while upcast_from_mxfp_torch keeps Inf (TODO in kernel); NaN through tl.clamp.
